source_doc: Derry & Ramsey to Groves, 'Summary of Target Committee Meetings on 10 and 11 May 1945', 12 May 1945, RG 77 MED TS File 5d; NSA Doc. 11
source_page: PDF p4 (doc p4), para 6A(1); p5 para 6B
quote: Kyoto - This target is an urban industrial area with a population of 1,000,000. It is the former capital of Japan ... (Classified as an AA Target)
notes: Recommended as first of 'first four choices' (6B). Psychological reason, para 7B: 'Kyoto has the advantage of the people being more highly intelligent and hence better able to appreciate the significance of the weapon.'

target_class: army depot / port of embarkation in urban industrial area
source_doc: Derry & Ramsey to Groves, 'Summary of Target Committee Meetings on 10 and 11 May 1945', 12 May 1945, RG 77 MED TS File 5d; NSA Doc. 11
source_page: PDF p4 (doc p4), para 6A(2); p5 para 6B
quote: Hiroshima - This is an important army depot and port of embarkation in the middle of an urban industrial area. It is a good radar target ... (Classified as an AA Target)
notes: Reasons also stated: city size allows extensive damage; adjacent hills 'likely to produce a focusing effect'; 'Due to rivers it is not a good incendiary target.' In 'first four choices' (6B).

source_doc: Derry & Ramsey to Groves, 'Summary of Target Committee Meetings on 10 and 11 May 1945', 12 May 1945, RG 77 MED TS File 5d; NSA Doc. 11
quote: Yokohama - This target is an important urban industrial area which has so far been untouched. ... (Classified as an A Target)
notes: Reasons: aircraft manufacture, machine tools, docks, electrical equipment, oil refineries; disadvantage: heaviest anti-aircraft concentration in Japan; advantage as bad-weather alternative far from other targets. In 'first four choices'.

source_doc: Derry & Ramsey to Groves, 'Summary of Target Committee Meetings on 10 and 11 May 1945', 12 May 1945, RG 77 MED TS File 5d; NSA Doc. 11
quote: Kokura Arsenal - This is one of the largest arsenals in Japan and is surrounded by urban industrial structures. ... (Classified as an A Target)
notes: Arsenal 4100' x 2000'; important for light ordnance, anti-aircraft and beach head defense materials. In 'first four choices'.

source_doc: Derry & Ramsey to Groves, 'Summary of Target Committee Meetings on 10 and 11 May 1945', 12 May 1945, RG 77 MED TS File 5d; NSA Doc. 11
quote: Niigata - This is a port of embarkation on the N.W. coast of Honshu. Its importance is increasing as other ports are damaged. ... (Classified as a B Target)
notes: One of five targets the Air Forces would reserve, but NOT among the recommended 'first four choices' (6B) -> selected=0 at this stage only; reinstated 28 May.

source_doc: Derry & Ramsey to Groves, 'Summary of Target Committee Meetings on 10 and 11 May 1945', 12 May 1945, RG 77 MED TS File 5d; NSA Doc. 11
source_page: PDF p5 (doc p5), para 6A(6); PDF p6 para 7B
quote: The possibility of bombing the Emperor's palace was discussed. It was agreed that we should not recommend it but that any action for this bombing should come from authorities on military policy.
notes: Located in Tokyo. Para 7B: 'The Emperor's palace in Tokyo has a greater fame than any other target but is of least strategic value.'

source_doc: Col. John Stone to Gen. Arnold, 'Groves Project', 24 July 1945, RG 77 MED TS Files 5b/5e; NSA Doc. 60B
quote: Hiroshima (population 350,000) is an "Army" city; a major POE; has large QM and supply depots; has considerable industry and several small shipyards.
notes: Para 1b: 'The following targets have been selected: Hiroshima, Kokura, Niigata and Nagasaki.' Memo numbers them (1) Hiroshima (2) Nagasaki (3) Kokura (4) Niigata (not stated as priority). Para 1c: all four 'believed to contain large numbers of key Japanese industrialists and political figures who have sought refuge'.

source_doc: Col. John Stone to Gen. Arnold, 'Groves Project', 24 July 1945, RG 77 MED TS Files 5b/5e; NSA Doc. 60B

notes: Para 2: 'Additional bombs will be delivered on the above targets as soon as made ready by the project staff.' Same text as proposed directive in WAR 37683 (Doc. 60C, 24 July), which spells 'Niigata'.
